title: This Town Has Been on Fire Underground for 64 Years #history #shorts
description:
In May 1962, Centralia, Pennsylvania, set its town dump on fire to clean it up before Memorial Day. The dump sat in an old strip-mine pit, and the fire most likely got into a seam of coal. It has been burning in the old mine tunnels under the town ever since.

Facts used: the fire has burned beneath Centralia since at least May 27, 1962, when the borough had five volunteer firefighters burn the landfill in an abandoned strip-mine pit (the exact cause is still debated). Years of trenching and flushing failed. On Feb. 14, 1981, 12-year-old Todd Domboski fell into a smoking sinkhole in his grandmother's yard; he held on to tree roots until his cousin pulled him out, and the hole was later found to be about 150 feet deep. Congress set aside about $42 million to buy out and move the town; the state took the remaining properties by eminent domain in 1992; the Postal Service retired the 17927 ZIP code in 2002; in 2013 the last residents won the right to stay for life. The 2020 census counted 5 people. At its current rate the fire could burn for another 250 years.

The scenes are an animated dramatization.
